notes.2: Makes 24 rolls in two baking dishes. Knead the dough in two halves.

move.title: Every roll the same weight
move.body: Rolls that weigh the same rise and bake the same. Today you'll weigh the dough, divide it into 12 pieces within a tenth of an ounce of each other, and shape each into a smooth, tight ball. Two or three become small knots or braids, practice for next week's challah.

callback.body: Pita's balls only had to roll out flat. A roll keeps its shape, so each ball needs a tight, smooth skin to hold its gas and rise up instead of spreading out.

why.title: Why an egg
why.body: Egg adds fat and protein. The fat makes the crumb soft, and the protein helps the rolls hold their shape and brown. It's a step toward challah, which has more.

why.title: Why weigh
why.body: By eye, pieces can differ by a third. The small ones overbake while the big ones are still doughy in the middle. On a scale, all 12 finish together.

why.title: A tight skin
why.body: Cupping a piece and rolling it against the counter stretches its outside into a smooth, tight skin. The skin holds the gas in, so the roll rises up and comes out round.

why.title: Rolls that touch
why.body: Spaced so they just touch after rising, the rolls hold each other up and bake with soft sides that pull apart.

why.title: 190°F inside
why.body: At 190°F, the crumb in the center has set. A golden top can come before that, so check the middle roll, which bakes last.

wrong.sign: The rolls came out different sizes
wrong.fix: Weigh each piece and pinch dough from heavy ones onto light ones until they're within a tenth of an ounce.

wrong.sign: The tops are wrinkled or torn
wrong.fix: The skin was stretched too far. Roll the next ball gently, just until the top is smooth.

wrong.sign: A ball won't hold its shape
wrong.fix: Cup it under your hand and roll it on a bare spot of counter, not on flour. A little stickiness gives it grip.
Bake 3 more minutes and check again. Lay foil over the top if it's getting too dark.

quiz.q: Why weigh each piece of dough?
choices: So all the rolls bake through at the same time
quiz.explain: Small rolls overbake while big ones are still doughy.

quiz.q: Which roll do you check with the thermometer?
choices: One in the middle of the dish
quiz.explain: The middle ones are shaded by their neighbors and bake last.

ingredients.text: a little more, for the bowl and dish

steps.text: Warm the milk in the measuring cup in the microwave for about 40 seconds. Stir it and check it with the thermometer. It should read 105 to 110°F.
steps.tip: Too hot? Let it sit a minute and check again.

steps.text: Pour the milk into the large bowl. Stir in the sugar, then sprinkle the yeast over the top. Leave it alone to bloom.
steps.look: Foam on top, and it smells like bread.

steps.text: Crack in the egg and beat it in with the fork.
Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Add the 4 tablespoons of softened butter, the salt, and the flour. Stir with the wooden spoon until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg and raw flour.

steps.text: Dust the counter with flour and turn the dough out. Knead it until it's smooth and stretchy and passes the windowpane test.
steps.look: A small piece stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing.

steps.text: Butter the bowl, put the dough in, and turn it once to coat it. Cover with a towel and leave it somewhere warm until it doubles.
steps.look: Doubled. A floured finger pressed in leaves a dent that stays.

steps.text: Butter the baking dish. Weigh the whole dough on the scale and divide the weight by 12. Cut the dough into 12 pieces with the knife, weighing each one. Pinch dough from heavy pieces onto light ones until they're all within a tenth of an ounce.
steps.tip: Write the target weight down. It's usually about 2¼ ounces.

steps.text: Cup a piece under your palm on a bare spot of counter and roll it in small circles until the top is smooth and tight. Shape 9 or 10 rolls this way and set them in the dish in rows, a little apart.

Shape the last 2 or 3 pieces as knots or small braids. For a knot, roll a piece into an 8-inch rope, tie it in a loose knot, and tuck the ends under. For a braid, cut a piece into 3, roll each into a thin rope, and braid them, pinching the ends. Fit them into the dish with the others.
steps.tip: This is practice for next week. Even if they're lopsided, they'll bake into good rolls.

steps.text: Cover the dish loosely with the towel and let the rolls proof. Heat the oven to 375°F while they do.
steps.look: Puffy, and the rolls are touching each other.

steps.text: Bake the rolls until they're golden. If the tops brown fast, lay a sheet of foil loosely over them.

With oven mitts, pull the dish out partway. Push the thermometer into the side of a roll in the middle of the dish, so the tip is in its center. They're done at 190°F. If it's lower, bake 3 more minutes and check again.
Turn off the oven. Set the dish on the cooling rack. Melt the 2 tablespoons of butter in the small bowl in the microwave, about 20 seconds, and brush it over the tops.
Let the rolls cool in the dish before pulling them apart.
steps.tip: Leftover rolls keep in a bag at room temperature for 2 days, or in the freezer for 3 months.
